definition: Distributed R is an open source, high-performance platform for the R language.
details: It splits tasks between multiple processing nodes to reduce execution time and analyze large data sets. Distributed R enhances R by adding distributed data structures, parallelism primitives to run functions on distributed data, a task scheduler, and multiple data loaders. It is mostly used to implement distributed versions of machine learning tasks. Distributed R is written in C++ and R, and retains the familiar look and feel of R. As of February 2015, Hewlett-Packard (HP) provides enterprise support for Distributed R with proprietary additions such as a fast data loader from the Vertica database.

explainer.lead: Distributed R lets familiar R programs work across several processing nodes instead of just one. By splitting data and computation, it can shorten execution time and make large-scale machine-learning analysis more practical while preserving R's look and feel.

tiers.eli5: Imagine one person trying to check a huge stack of worksheets. Distributed R is like sharing the stack among several people, letting them work at the same time, and bringing their answers together, while still giving instructions in a familiar way.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use R-like code with distributed data structures and parallelism primitives, while the task scheduler coordinates work across processing nodes and loaders bring in data. It is mainly applied to distributed machine-learning tasks on large data sets. HP's fast Vertica loader was a proprietary enterprise addition, not part of the open-source core.
tiers.paperLevel: Given data D and computation f, Distributed R distributes D across processing nodes N1 through Nk and schedules f over the distributed data to reduce execution time and support larger data sets. The platform comprises distributed data structures, parallelism primitives, a task scheduler, and multiple data loaders, implemented in C++ and R. HP's enterprise offering added proprietary components, including a fast Vertica database loader.

explainer.example: A large table is loaded and divided across several processing nodes. A distributed machine-learning routine runs its calculations on the different portions in parallel and produces a result without requiring one R process to handle the entire table alone.

explainer.intuition: A single R process can struggle when data and computation become too large or slow. Distributed R spreads both across multiple processing nodes so they can work in parallel without abandoning the familiar R experience.
howItWorks: Data loaders bring data into the platform.
Distributed data structures hold data across processing nodes.
Parallelism primitives run functions on that distributed data.
A task scheduler coordinates the tasks among the nodes.
Parallel execution reduces running time and supports analysis of large data sets.
explainer.whyItMatters: It extends R toward large-data analysis by combining parallel execution with distributed data handling. Its familiar interface lets users approach distributed machine learning without switching to an entirely different-looking language.
misconceptions: It is not a replacement for R; it enhances R while retaining its familiar look and feel.
It is not written only in R; its implementation uses both C++ and R.
HP's fast Vertica loader was a proprietary enterprise addition, not a feature of the open-source platform itself.
